name: SwiftMatch AI — SME Opportunity Matching
purpose: Rank verified youth-owned township SMEs against a corporate procurement request and explain every ranking so a human procurement officer can audit it.
humanInTheLoop: The engine produces a shortlist, never an award. A procurement officer makes the selection.
The SME chooses to accept, decline, or ask a question on WhatsApp. Nothing is committed on their behalf.
Claude-generated text (RFQ extraction, audit narrative, WhatsApp draft) is editable before use and labelled as AI-generated.

data.smeProfiles: 6 synthetic supplier profiles modelled on real Kasi-eCo marketplace categories (leather, timber, eco-packaging, workwear, metal, ceramics). Names, phone numbers and compliance flags are fictional. No real personal information is processed in this prototype.
data.rfqs: 3 synthetic corporate RFQs written for the demo. Buyer names are illustrative.

scoringInputs: Requirement text vs SME capability text (sentence embeddings + tag overlap)
Monthly production capacity and average turnaround vs required quantity and deadline
Mandatory statutory checks selected by the buyer (CIPC, SARS Tax PIN, B-BBEE level, COIDA, youth ownership)
Haversine distance from the resolved delivery site
Kasi-eCo rating and verified order count
excludedInputs: Owner age, gender, name, ethnicity or language — never used in scoring
Any data the SME has not consented to share
biasAndFairness: Weights are fixed, published and identical for every supplier.
Hard compliance filters are only those the buyer explicitly selects; optional checks (e.g. COIDA) affect advice, not eligibility.
Reputation is capped at 10% so new entrants are not locked out by incumbents' order history.
Ineligible suppliers are still shown with the exact missing document so they can fix it (right of response), rather than silently excluded.
privacy: Phone numbers and emails are masked on all corporate screens until the SME accepts an opportunity (POPIA purpose limitation).
Embeddings run on-device; SME profile text is not sent to a third-party embedding API.
Only the RFQ text and the SME's business (not personal) fields are sent to Claude, and only when an API key is configured.
limitations: Prototype dataset is tiny and synthetic; scores are not validated against real award outcomes.
Embedding similarity measures text relatedness, not product quality. A sample and site visit are still required.
Compliance flags are self-declared seed data; production would verify against CIPC/SARS APIs.
The location resolver uses a fixed gazetteer of South African cities; unknown sites default to Sandton and are flagged.
B-BBEE point estimates are indicative and depend on the buyer's total measured spend.
evaluation: Run `npm run eval` in /server to reproduce Top-1 accuracy and MRR on the held-out RFQ test set (eval/testset.json).
